parts.instructions: Listen to the phone call and choose the best answer A, B, C or D (Questions L1–L5).
parts.context: Chloe, a video editor, phones Marcus at Apex PCs to order a new computer.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Apex PCs, Marcus speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Hi. I'm a video editor, and I'd like to order a new computer. My old one is far too slow for 4K video.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: No problem. Let's start with the processor. For 4K editing, I'd recommend our twelve-core processor. It runs at four point two gigahertz.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: That sounds good. What about memory? My old computer has sixteen gigabytes.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: For video, you need at least thirty-two, but I'd suggest sixty-four gigabytes so that you can run several programs at once.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: OK, sixty-four, then. And storage? My video files are huge.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: I'd suggest a two terabyte drive for your programs and current projects, and a large external drive for old projects. That's cheaper than putting everything inside the computer.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Good idea. Do I need a special graphics card?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Yes, definitely. Video software uses the graphics card to make editing faster. Our best one has sixteen gigabytes of its own memory.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Great. How much will all that cost?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Without the external drive, it comes to two thousand three hundred and fifty pounds. We can build it in five working days.

script.speaker: Chloe
script.text: Perfect. Could you send me the details by email?

questions.stem: Why does Chloe want a new computer?

options.text: Her old computer is too slow for 4K video.
She wants to play computer games.
She is starting a new company.

questions.explanation: Chloe: "My old one is far too slow for 4K video."

questions.stem: How fast is the processor that Marcus recommends?
questions.explanation: "It runs at four point two gigahertz." Số 12 là số nhân (twelve-core), không phải tốc độ.

questions.stem: How much memory does Chloe decide to have?
questions.explanation: Marcus gợi ý 64 GB và Chloe đồng ý: "OK, sixty-four, then." 16 GB là máy cũ, 32 GB là mức tối thiểu.

questions.stem: Why does Marcus suggest an external drive for Chloe's old projects?

options.text: It is faster than an internal drive.
It is easier to carry to work.
The new computer has no space for a drive.
It is cheaper than putting everything inside the computer.

questions.explanation: Marcus: "That's cheaper than putting everything inside the computer."

questions.stem: How much will the computer cost without the external drive?
questions.explanation: "it comes to two thousand three hundred and fifty pounds" = £2,350.

parts.context: Ben explains three ways to take a screenshot on a Windows laptop.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Hi, I'm Ben, and in today's video I'm going to show you three easy ways to take a screenshot on a Windows laptop.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: The first way is the quickest. Just press the Print Screen key. On most keyboards, it's in the top right-hand corner. This copies the whole screen. Then open a document and press Control and V to paste the picture.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: The second way is better if you only need part of the screen. Hold down the Windows key and the Shift key, and then press S. The screen goes grey. Now choose the part you want with your mouse. The picture is copied, so you can paste it into an email or a document.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: The third way saves the picture as a file. Press the Windows key and Print Screen together. The screen goes dark for a second, and the screenshot is saved automatically in the Screenshots folder, inside your Pictures folder.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Finally, a useful tip: if you need a screenshot of a menu that disappears when you press a key, use the Snipping Tool and set a delay of five seconds. That gives you time to open the menu. See you next time!

questions.stem: Where is the Print Screen key on most keyboards?
questions.explanation: "On most keyboards, it's in the top right-hand corner."

questions.stem: Which keys do you press to paste the picture into a document?
questions.explanation: "Then open a document and press Control and V to paste the picture."

questions.stem: What colour does the screen go after you press Windows, Shift and S?
questions.explanation: "Hold down the Windows key and the Shift key, and then press S. The screen goes grey."

questions.stem: What is the name of the folder inside Pictures where screenshots are saved automatically?
questions.explanation: "the screenshot is saved automatically in the Screenshots folder, inside your Pictures folder".

questions.stem: How long is the delay that Ben suggests in the Snipping Tool?
questions.explanation: "use the Snipping Tool and set a delay of five seconds".

grammar.stem: A millisecond is one ______ of a second.
grammar.explanation: Tiền tố milli- nghĩa là một phần nghìn: 1 millisecond = 1/1.000 giây. Một phần triệu là micro-, một phần tỷ là nano-.

grammar.stem: The company sold 2,500,000 laptops last year. How do we say '2,500,000'?
grammar.explanation: Khi đọc số, million, hundred, thousand đứng sau số đếm không thêm -s: two million five hundred thousand.

grammar.stem: Could you ______ the printer on, please? I need to print a report.
grammar.explanation: Lời yêu cầu lịch sự: Could you + động từ nguyên mẫu không "to": "Could you switch the printer on?".

grammar.stem: Take the DVD ______ the drive and put it back in its case.
grammar.explanation: Câu hai tân ngữ: take + tân ngữ 1 + out of + tân ngữ 2 (lấy cái gì ra khỏi đâu).

options.text: Plug into the audio socket the headphones.
Into the audio socket plug the headphones.
Plug the headphones into the audio socket.
Plug the headphones the audio socket into.

grammar.explanation: Trật tự câu hai tân ngữ: động từ + tân ngữ 1 (the headphones) + giới từ (into) + tân ngữ 2 (the audio socket).

grammar.stem: The video won't play ______ the file is damaged.
grammar.explanation: Vế sau (the file is damaged) là lý do nên dùng "because" + mệnh đề. "so that" chỉ mục đích; for / to không đi với mệnh đề.

grammar.stem: Double click the title bar ______ the window.
grammar.explanation: Chỉ mục đích bằng to + động từ nguyên mẫu: "Double click the title bar to maximise the window".

vocabulary.stem: ______ on the file and choose 'Rename' from the menu that appears.
vocabulary.explanation: Right-click (nhấp chuột phải) để mở menu các lệnh, ví dụ Rename (đổi tên).

vocabulary.stem: Give the document a clear ______, such as 'Sales_May', so that you can find it easily later.
vocabulary.explanation: Filename (tên tệp) là tên bạn đặt cho một tệp.

vocabulary.stem: To print the document, choose 'Print' from the File ______.
vocabulary.explanation: Menu (trình đơn) là danh sách các lệnh trên màn hình; menu File có lệnh Print.

vocabulary.stem: If the screen freezes and the mouse doesn't work, ______ the computer.
vocabulary.explanation: Restart (khởi động lại) là cho máy chạy lại sau khi đã dừng, ví dụ khi màn hình bị treo.

vocabulary.stem: Type your question in the search box and ______ the Enter key.
vocabulary.explanation: Press (nhấn) một phím hoặc nút để máy thực hiện việc gì.

vocabulary.stem: This game has amazing 3-D ______: the cars and buildings look almost real.
vocabulary.explanation: Graphics (đồ hoạ) là hình ảnh tạo ra trong chương trình máy tính để thể hiện đồ vật.

vocabulary.explanation: Virtual reality goggles (kính thực tế ảo) là kính đặc biệt đeo lên mắt để thấy môi trường do máy tính tạo ra. Headphones đeo trên tai.

passage.title: Hillside School Moves to Open Source
paragraphs: Last year, Hillside School in Leeds had a problem. Its 300 student laptops were six years old, and the proprietary operating system on them was going to stop receiving security updates. New laptops for every student would cost about £150,000, and the school could not afford that.

The school's IT manager, Ravi Patel, suggested a different solution. Instead of buying new machines, the school installed a free open source operating system on the old laptops. Because the open source system needs less memory, the laptops ran faster than before. The school only had to buy extra 4 GB memory modules for 120 of the laptops, so that they could run video software. Each module cost £15.

Ravi and two technicians did the work during the summer holiday. First, they backed up the students' files to the school server. Then they installed the new system on each laptop from a USB stick. Each installation took about twenty-five minutes, and the whole project took three weeks.

Not everyone was happy at first. Some teachers had to learn new programs, and the school's exam software only works on the old proprietary system, so the school kept ten laptops with the old system for exams. But after six months, most students and teachers say that the laptops work better than before. The school saved more than £140,000, and it now plans to use some of the money to build a new media room.

To install the new operating system
Because the old modules were broken

passage.title: Headphones: Which Type Is Right for You?
paragraphs: Wired headphones plug into the headphone socket of your phone or computer. They are usually cheaper than wireless ones, and you never have to charge them. However, many new phones do not have a headphone socket, so you may need an adapter.

Wireless headphones connect to your device by Bluetooth. They are more comfortable for sport because there is no cable. Most models play music for 20 to 30 hours before you need to charge them. The sound quality is good, but professional sound engineers still prefer wired headphones because there is no delay.

Noise-cancelling headphones are useful on trains and planes. They have small microphones that listen to the noise around you and cancel it. They cost more than normal headphones, and the noise-cancelling function uses extra battery power.

If you work in an open-plan office, choose headphones with a built-in microphone, so that you can join online meetings without a separate headset. Before you buy, always try the headphones on in the shop, because comfort matters as much as sound.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "many new phones do not have a headphone socket".

questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: "Most models play music for 20 to 30 hours before you need to charge them."

questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: "professional sound engineers still prefer wired headphones because there is no delay".

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "the noise-cancelling function uses extra battery power".

parts.instructions: Give instructions for using a computer. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: A classmate wants to share a file with you from their online storage, for example Google Drive, but does not know how. Explain the steps. Use imperatives, sequence words (first, then, next, after that, finally) and at least one softener (could you…?, just).
cues: open the online storage website / log in
find the file / right-click on it
type the other person's email address
requiredGrammar: Imperatives with sequence words: First, … Then, … Next, … After that, … Finally, …
parts.sampleAnswer: Sharing a file is really easy. First, open the website in your browser and log in with your email and password. Then find the file you want to share. You can just type the filename in the search box at the top. Next, right-click on the file and select 'Share' from the menu. A small window appears. After that, could you type my email address in the box? Make sure you spell it correctly. Then choose 'Viewer' if you only want me to read the file, or 'Editor' if you want me to change it too. For our project, please choose 'Editor', because we both need to write in it. Finally, click 'Send'. I'll get an email with a link to the file in a few seconds.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Your manager wants to use the office's old desktop computers for two more years. Explain to her which parts you want to add or change, how you will connect or install each one and why it is needed. Use sentences with two objects (put … into …, connect … to …, plug … into …) and reason or purpose (to…, so that…, because…, for…).
cues: 8 GB more memory: put the module into the empty DIMM slot / so that staff can open several programs
a solid state drive instead of the old hard disk / because it starts programs much faster
a second monitor: connect it to the video socket / for working with two documents
a webcam: plug it into a USB port / to join video meetings with clients
requiredGrammar: Sentences with two objects: put … into …, connect … to …, plug … into …
Reason and purpose: to + verb, so that + clause, because + clause, for + noun / -ing
parts.sampleAnswer: I think we can use the old computers for two more years if we change a few parts. First, I'd like to add eight gigabytes of memory. I'll put the new module into the empty DIMM slot on the motherboard, so that staff can open several programs at the same time. Second, I want to replace the old hard disk with a solid state drive, because it starts programs much faster. Third, each person could have a second monitor. I'll connect it to the video socket on the back of the computer. It's very useful for working with two documents at once. Finally, we need webcams. I'll plug them into the USB ports to let staff join video meetings with clients. All of this is much cheaper than buying new computers.
